questions.question:
An application in the namespace `backend` must call the Service `web-ui` (port `3000`) in the namespace `frontend` by DNS.

1. Write the **fully qualified** DNS name of the Service to `/tmp/exam/q1/dns-name.txt` on `ckad9999`
2. Create a Pod `dns-test` in the namespace `backend` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`)
3. From `dns-test`, run `nslookup` on that name and save the output to `/tmp/exam/q1/nslookup.txt`

verification.description: dns-name.txt contains the Service FQDN
dns-test Pod runs in backend
nslookup.txt shows the Service resolving to its ClusterIP

questions.question:
The Deployment `payment-service` in the namespace `payments` was updated several times, and the latest update broke it.

1. Inspect the rollout history and find the revision that introduced the problem. Write that revision number to `/tmp/exam/q2/bad-revision.txt` on `ckad9999`
2. Roll back to the last **working** revision
3. Make sure all `3` replicas are Ready

verification.description: bad-revision.txt names the broken revision
payment-service rolled back to nginx:1.25 with 3 Ready replicas

questions.question:
In the namespace `app-secrets`:

1. Create a Secret `db-creds` with the keys `username=dbuser`, `password=secret123` and `database=appdb`
2. Create a Deployment `db-client` (1 replica, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that exposes them as **environment variables** `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DB_DATABASE` (not as files)

The application must not print the values to its logs.

verification.description: Secret db-creds has the three keys
db-client references the Secret through env vars, no secret volumes
Pod sees the values and does not log them

questions.question:
The control-plane node `k3d-cluster-server-0` carries the taint `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule`.

Create a DaemonSet `monitoring-agent` in the namespace `monitoring` that runs on **every** node, including the control plane:

- Pod label `app=monitoring-agent`
- Container `agent`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'while true; do sleep 3600; done'` (stands in for a real agent such as `datadog/agent`)
- Tolerate exactly that control-plane taint (key `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane`, effect `NoSchedule`)

verification.description: DaemonSet tolerates the control-plane taint
An agent Pod is Ready on every node

questions.question:
Users report that the API server seems slow. The control-plane node is not reachable over SSH in this lab, so check it through the API:

1. Save the output of the API server's **verbose readiness endpoint** to `/tmp/exam/q5/readyz.txt` on `ckad9999`
2. Find the port the API server listens on, by looking at the endpoints of the `kubernetes` Service in the `default` namespace, and write it to `/tmp/exam/q5/apiserver-port.txt`

verification.description: readyz.txt contains the verbose readiness checks
apiserver-port.txt contains the API server port

questions.question:
The Deployment `config-app` in the namespace `config-reload` reads its mode from the ConfigMap `app-config` through the environment variable `APP_MODE`, which is only read when a container starts.

1. Change the key `APP_MODE` in `app-config` to `production`
2. Additionally mount the ConfigMap as a volume named `config` at `/etc/app` in the container (no `subPath`, so future file changes are picked up automatically)
3. Make sure all running Pods use the new value, without deleting the Deployment

verification.description: ConfigMap updated and mounted without subPath
All Pods see APP_MODE=production in env and file

questions.question:
Set up workload priorities:

1. Create a PriorityClass `critical` with value `1000` and a PriorityClass `standard` with value `100` (neither is the global default)
2. In the namespace `priority-lab`, create the Pods `critical-pod-1` and `critical-pod-2` using `critical`, and `standard-pod` using `standard` (all image `nginx:1.25`)

When a node runs short on resources, lower-priority Pods are preempted first.

verification.description: PriorityClasses have the right values
Pods run with the expected priorities

questions.question:
The legacy application `legacy-app` (label `app=legacy-app`, container port `3000`) in the namespace `legacy` must be reachable from outside the cluster without an Ingress.

Create a Service `legacy-app` of the appropriate type that:

- listens on Service port `8080` and forwards to container port `3000`
- is exposed on every node at port `30808`

(NodePorts must be in the range 30000-32767, so a node port of 8080 is not possible.)

verification.description: Service legacy-app is a NodePort 8080 -> 3000 on 30808
The app answers on a node IP at port 30808

questions.question:
In the namespace `backups`, create a CronJob `backup-job` that:

- runs every day at `2:00 AM`
- uses container `backup`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'echo backup done'`
- keeps only the last `3` successful Jobs
- is **suspended** (it must not run until someone resumes it)

verification.description: CronJob schedule, history and container
CronJob is suspended

questions.question:
`kubeadm certs renew` needs control-plane access, which this lab does not provide, so practice the Kubernetes certificate API instead. A private key and a certificate signing request for the user `john` were generated in `/tmp/exam/q10/` (`john.key`, `john.csr`).

1. Create a CertificateSigningRequest `john` from `john.csr` with signer `kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client`, usage `client auth` and an expiration of `86400` seconds
2. Approve it
3. Save the issued certificate (PEM) to `/tmp/exam/q10/john.crt`

verification.description: CSR john uses the right signer, usage and expiration
CSR approved and certificate issued
john.crt is the issued certificate for CN=john

questions.question:
The Deployment `web-app` in the namespace `pdb-lab` runs `10` replicas (label `app=web-app`) and must never lose more than `2` Pods at once during voluntary disruptions such as node drains.

Create a PodDisruptionBudget `app-pdb` that enforces this using `maxUnavailable`.

verification.description: PDB app-pdb selects app=web-app with maxUnavailable 2
PDB currently allows exactly 2 disruptions

questions.question:
Your team installed a CustomResourceDefinition for `Database` objects.

1. Find the CRD and its API group/version
2. Create a `Database` named `prod-db` in the namespace `crd-db` with `spec.engine: postgres`, `spec.version: "16"` and `spec.storageGB: 20`
3. Delete the obsolete `Database` named `legacy-db` in `crd-db`

verification.description: Database prod-db exists with the right spec
Database legacy-db is deleted (CRD kept)

questions.question:
The namespace `restricted-apps` enforces the Pod Security Standard `restricted`. A legacy Pod must run as **root**, which that level forbids. Pod Security Admission has no per-Pod exceptions, so isolate it in its own namespace instead:

1. Create a namespace `privileged-apps` that enforces the `baseline` level
2. Run a Pod `privileged-pod` there (image `nginx:1.25`) with `securityContext.runAsUser: 0`
3. Leave `restricted-apps` unchanged, so it still rejects Pods that run as root

verification.description: privileged-apps enforces baseline and privileged-pod runs as root
restricted-apps still enforces restricted

questions.question:
Configure dynamic provisioning:

1. Create a StorageClass `ssd-provisioner` using the cluster's provisioner `rancher.io/local-path`, with `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer` and `reclaimPolicy: Delete`
2. In the namespace `dyn-storage`, create a PVC `my-ssd-claim` requesting `20Gi` (`ReadWriteOnce`) from that class
3. Create a Pod `app-using-ssd` (image `nginx:1.25`) that mounts the claim at `/usr/share/nginx/html` (volume name `ssd-volume`)

Confirm that a PersistentVolume was created automatically and bound.

verification.description: StorageClass ssd-provisioner is correct
PVC is Bound to a dynamically provisioned PV
app-using-ssd mounts the claim and runs

questions.question:
Set up resource governance for the namespace `batch-jobs`:

1. A ResourceQuota `batch-jobs-quota` with `limits.cpu: 10` and `limits.memory: 20Gi`
2. A LimitRange `batch-jobs-limits` for type `Container` with `min` CPU `500m` / memory `256Mi` and `max` CPU `4` / memory `8Gi`
   (also set `default` limits of CPU `1` / memory `1Gi` and `defaultRequest` of CPU `500m` / memory `256Mi`, so Pods without resources are admitted)

Then verify that a Pod with a container asking for `6` CPUs is rejected.

verification.description: ResourceQuota batch-jobs-quota is correct
LimitRange batch-jobs-limits is correct
A 6 CPU Pod is rejected, a Pod without resources is admitted
